finding.title: Split the scheduler test files that exceed the AG-3 400-line hand-written-file cap
finding.rule: AG-3 [P] — hand-written Dart files (lib AND test) stay under 400 lines

evidence.quote: /// Unit tests for the SefariaRefMatcher domain service.
/// Logic tests — scheduler_providers.dart branches NOT covered by

finding.why: coding-standards.md's own AG-3 rationale is 'oversized files exceed per-file agent read budgets ... become dumping grounds' — confirmed by this audit, which needed multiple full-file reads north of 950-1100 lines to review two of these (scheduler_providers_test.dart at 1092 lines, sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart at 1010, scheduler_all_daily_tasks_test.dart at 957, scheduler_providers_branches_test.dart at 684, scheduler_screen_l1_test.dart at 677; verified via wc -l). All five are internally well-organized (clear group()/comment-banner sections), so splitting is low-risk.
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing group()/comment-banner boundaries (e.g. scheduler_providers_test.dart's 10 unrelated groups — SchedulerTaskSectionNotifier, SchedulerGroupedView, clockProvider, SkippedTasks, previouslySkippedRefsProvider, paceStatusProvider x2, overdueCountForCurriculumProvider, allDailyTasksProvider, firstTaskInTrackForCategoryProvider, 2 enums — map cleanly onto 3-4 files by provider), keeping each under 400 lines. Wire coding-standards.md's own specified checker (find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400') into make audit as warn-only first.
acceptance_criteria: The AG-3 checker command from coding-standards.md returns none of these 5 paths.
make audit gains the AG-3 line-count check (warn-only per the doc's own enforcement note).

finding.title: Delete scheduler_screen_test.dart — its scenarios duplicate scheduler_screen_l1_test.dart
finding.rule: Fowler duplication lens / AG-5 mirrored-test-path ambiguity

evidence.quote: expect(find.text('All caught up! Great work!'), findsOneWidget);
expect(find.text('All caught up! Great work!'), findsOneWidget);

finding.why: 8 of scheduler_screen_test.dart's 9 tests (empty state, task-card rendering, summary count, singular count, loading indicator, error+retry, swipe-dismiss snackbar) assert the identical hardcoded English strings against the identical widget (SchedulerScreen) as tests already present in scheduler_screen_l1_test.dart (@Tags(['scheduler','l1'])), which is a strict superset: it additionally covers section filters, no-track-type-label checks, an he-locale smoke test, an R6-6 raw-exception-leak regression, and — unlike the older file, which only checks an InkWell exists — actually drives the view-toggle into GroupedDailyView and back. Every future copy change to the shared strings (e.g. an ARB wording tweak) must land in both files or one silently goes stale, and both files pay CI time re-testing the same states.
finding.recommendation: Delete scheduler_screen_test.dart after folding its one non-duplicated assertion (DailyTaskCard renders the correct per-curriculum ref label text, e.g. 'Mishnah Berakhot 1.1' / 'Bavli Berakhot 2a') into scheduler_screen_l1_test.dart's flat-list test if that content check isn't covered elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Only one *_test.dart file exercises SchedulerScreen top-to-bottom, or the two files have non-overlapping, clearly-named scopes.
Diff review confirms no asserted behavior is lost after removal.

finding.title: Fix the sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart sortOrder test that cannot verify its own claim
finding.rule: TQ-8 (assertion must match what the source can actually do wrong)

evidence.quote: // Sets don't preserve insertion order, but the function sorts before

finding.why: leafChildrenForContainer returns Set<String>, so any internal sort is erased before the caller sees it; the test's own comment admits this and falls back to containsAll (membership only, no order check), so the test cannot fail if the production sort() call were deleted entirely — its name promises an ordering guarantee the assertion never checks.
finding.recommendation: Rename the test to describe what it actually checks (all three leaves present), or — if callers genuinely depend on order (resolveIndexedUnitRefs re-sorts independently, suggesting they don't) — change the return type to an ordered List and assert order for real.
acceptance_criteria: Test name matches its assertion, or the assertion is strengthened to check real order via a List-returning API.

finding.title: Relocate test/scheduler/*.dart into the mirrored test/features/ tree (AG-5) — no lib/scheduler/ exists to mirror

evidence.quote: /// Overdue projection characterisation tests — invariants O1, O2, O3, O7.
/// Overdue durability invariants — O4, O5, O6.

finding.why: test/scheduler/ matches none of the documented test/ subdirectories (story_acceptance/, core/, features/, integration/, helpers/, fixtures/, mocks/) and there is no lib/scheduler/ to mirror (only lib/features/scheduler/). This audit had to specifically search outside test/features/scheduler/ to find 2,087 lines of real, high-quality regression coverage for domain/projection/* and notification_providers.dart's reminderSyncEffect — the exact discoverability failure AG-5 exists to prevent; a future agent adding an overdue-projection test would very plausibly duplicate coverage at the correct path instead of finding these.
finding.recommendation: git mv overdue_projection_test.dart and overdue_durability_test.dart to test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/; git mv overdue_notifications_test.dart to test/features/notifications/presentation/providers/ (it tests notification_providers.dart, not scheduler code); fix relative helper imports (../helpers/drift_memory.dart path depth).
acceptance_criteria: The 3 files resolve at mirrored paths under test/features/{scheduler,notifications}/...
make ci is green after the move (imports adjusted).

finding.title: Delete unused features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator.dart — dead code, duplicate class name, hardcoded English
finding.rule: AG-4 (duplicate top-level symbol names) / AG-6 (dead code)
finding.why: grep -rln "PaceIndicator(" lib/ and grep -rln "features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator.dart" lib/ both return zero hits outside the file's own definition — this PaceIndicator/ProjectedCompletionText pair is never built into any screen (curriculum_progress_screen.dart uses the DIFFERENT features/progress PaceIndicator instead). 91 lines of widget tests exist purely to exercise unreachable code, and the duplicate class name across two features is exactly the AG-4 hazard the standards name: a future agent asked to fix 'the pace indicator' can edit this file, believe the fix shipped, and see nothing change because it never renders.
finding.recommendation: Delete lib/features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator.dart and test/features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator_test.dart. If the scheduler screen is meant to show a pace indicator, wire this widget into scheduler_screen.dart and route its strings through the existing paceAhead/paceBehind/paceOnPace ARB keys (already used by features/progress's PaceIndicator), and rename to avoid the AG-4 clash.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rl "features/scheduler/presentation/widgets/pace_indicator.dart" lib/ test/ returns nothing (removed) or exactly one real screen caller (wired).
grep -rn "^class PaceIndicator" lib/ returns exactly one match repo-wide.
